Course overview

Know what you’re preparing for.

International cruise ships operate like floating resorts. Behind every guest experience are teams across food and beverage, guest services, housekeeping and culinary operations. This pathway helps students understand that workplace, communicate professionally and prepare for recruitment—without promising a job or bypassing employer selection.

Who this is for

  • Class 10/12 students exploring a first hospitality role
  • Graduates or diploma holders moving into guest service
  • Students who enjoy people-facing work and can adapt to a multicultural team
  • Applicants ready to work shifts and live onboard for a contract

Eligibility & readiness

Start with the criteria that can change your route.

These are general orientation points. Final admission and employer criteria vary by role and current regulations.

Medical standards: Eyesight, colour vision and physical standards apply where relevant, as per current DG Shipping guidelines and institution/employer requirements. Obtain proper medical advice before paying substantial fees.

01

Class 10 or Class 12 from a recognised board; role-specific requirements vary

02

Age criteria depend on the employer and role; discuss your profile before applying

03

Communicative English and customer-service aptitude

04

Medically fit for the intended role; meet employer and applicable flag/port requirements

05

Curriculum

What your preparation covers.

[CONFIRM: Validate module names, hours and practical facilities against the actual delivered course before launch.]

01

Cruise industry orientation

Ship departments, guest journey, hierarchy, contracts and life away from home.

02

Professional English & communication

Guest conversations, pronunciation practice, listening and workplace vocabulary.

03

Food & beverage foundations

Service sequence, table setup, menu awareness, hygiene and responsible service.

04

Housekeeping & guest services

Cabin standards, privacy, requests, complaints and inter-department coordination.

05

Safety, grooming & workplace conduct

Personal presentation, cultural sensitivity, anti-harassment awareness and emergency orientation.

06

Interview & documentation preparation

CV, mock interviews, document folder, realistic employer research and offer checks.

Career outcomes & reality

Prepare for a pathway—not a promise.

Your next role depends on eligibility, recognised training where required, performance, documents and employer vacancies.

Possible directions

  • Entry-level food & beverage service
  • Housekeeping and cabin stewardship
  • Guest services support
  • Culinary and galley support
  • Shore-side hotels and resorts as an alternative pathway
Indicative industry ranges

What can you earn?

Entry-level cruise hospitality compensation is often discussed around ₹30,000–₹90,000 per month, with significant variation by role, company, contract, tips and prior experience. These are indicative industry ranges, not National Global Academy placement or salary guarantees. Confirm whether figures include benefits and what expenses you bear.

Read: Cruise Ship Jobs for Indians: Salary, Roles & How to Apply
For parents

Make the decision together, with the full picture.

A cruise contract can offer exposure and savings potential, but it also means months away, shared accommodation and demanding service hours. We encourage parents to attend counselling, review the complete cost sheet and understand that the academy’s role is training and career guidance—not guaranteed recruitment.

Straight answers

Cruise Hospitality: your questions, answered.

Eligibility, cost, safety and what happens next.

Can I join a cruise hospitality course after 12th?

Yes, Class 12 students can explore entry-level pathways. Employer age, English, medical and document requirements still apply. A counselling session should map your profile to suitable departments.

Do I need a hotel management degree?

Not for every entry-level role. Relevant skills, communication and experience can matter; some specialised or senior positions prefer hospitality qualifications.

Are cruise salaries tax-free?

Tax depends on your residential status, days outside India and current tax rules. Do not assume income is tax-free; consult a qualified tax professional.

Will the academy arrange my cruise job?

The academy provides training and career guidance. [CONFIRM: Describe verified recruitment assistance exactly.] No applicant should treat counselling or an interview opportunity as an employment guarantee.
